definitions.explanation: A short, memorable saying that expresses a general truth or piece of advice. Often attributed to a specific person or tradition.

examples.japanese: これは{有名|ゆうめい}な{格言|かくげん}だ。
{祖父|そふ}はよく{格言|かくげん}を{引用|いんよう}して{話|はな}した。
examples.english: My grandfather often spoke by quoting proverbs.

examples.japanese: 「{時|とき}は{金|かね}なり」という{格言|かくげん}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}で{知|し}られている。
examples.english: The maxim 'time is money' is known throughout the world.

notes: Distinguished from related words: {諺|ことわざ} (proverb) refers to folk sayings passed down through generations, while {格言|かくげん} tends to refer to more literary or attributed sayings. {名言|めいげん} (famous saying) emphasizes that the quote is well-known and often attributed to a specific person. Common collocations include {格言|かくげん}を{引用|いんよう}する (to quote an aphorism) and {格言|かくげん}{集|しゅう} (collection of maxims).
